evidence: src/infrastructure/http/RequestReader.ts: the RequestReader class (requiredString, optionalString) and BadRequestError handle reading and validating request input.
src/infrastructure/http/createApp.ts: createApp(controllers: Controllers) sets up express.json(), the routes, the 404 fallback and errorHandler.
src/infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts: statusFor() is the only place that maps ValidationError/BadRequestError/parse errors to 400, NotFoundError to 404 and ConflictError to 409.
errorHandler.ts imports BadRequestError from '../RequestReader' and uses the module's own error type, so it does not bypass that abstraction.
createApp.ts writes res.status(404).json({ error: 'Route not found' }) inline. This repeats errorHandler's { error } response shape, but it is minor and not a duplicated invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files belong to the HTTP adapter. RequestReader.ts turns raw request input into typed values and raises BadRequestError. createApp.ts sets up Express, the routes and the middleware. middleware/errorHandler.ts maps errors to HTTP status codes and JSON responses. The error-to-status rule lives only in statusFor and is not repeated anywhere else. errorHandler uses the module's own BadRequestError and does not match error messages or roll its own check. Two small points do not amount to a failure. First, the 404 fallback in createApp.ts writes the { error } JSON shape inline instead of going through errorHandler. That is a minor repeat of the response format, not of a business rule. Second, BadRequestError is declared in RequestReader.ts, not in a dedicated errors file. That is a placement choice and stays within the module.
